page.overview:
Who is Tolka?

Tolka is a tall, plain-looking young man with light hair and pale eyes. When he goes hunting, he dons a hoodie and a quiver on his back.

Tolka has been conditioned to believe that taking a life is not a serious matter thanks to his hunting trips with his master. After being questioned on whether he can kill a sixteen-year-old boy like an animal, Tolka affirms that he can do so.

Tolka is devoted to his master; being willing to kill another person so that she could retire peacefully, as well as wiping her mouth when she eats.

Tolka and his master are hunting in the woods when they come across a fox which he shoots with an arrow. He questions the point of the hunt they're on while his master repeatedly asks him whether he thinks he has taken a life or not. They return to their cottage and cook the fox. His master reveals that their next job is not a job to hunt a devil but to hunt and kill a sixteen-year-old boy, much like the fox they have just hunted and killed. Tolka swears to his master that he can kill. He makes a promise to her that, since she has just half a year left to live that he wants her to live her remaining days in a peaceful retirement.
